message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck works best with 4–8). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a “Reverse” changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard. You may also play a Wild or Wild Draw Four at any time. | | **Special Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw from the draw pile until you get a playable card. If you still can’t play after drawing, you pass. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have one card left, shout “UNO!” before your next player takes a turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of all cards left in opponents’ hands (0=0, 1–9=face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse=20, Wild/Wild Draw Four=50). | | **Scoring** | Keep a running total. First to reach the agreed‑upon score (commonly 500) wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – Even if you’re not playing a Wild, you need to know which color is active to decide what you can play. 2. **Use “Draw Two” and “Wild Draw Four” strategically** – Save them for when you’re about to win or when you’re in a tight spot. 3. **Watch opponents’ “UNO” calls** – If they forget, you can call them out and force them to draw two. 4. **Challenge a “Wild Draw Four”** – If you suspect the player had a matching color, you can challenge. If they were right, you draw four; if they were wrong, they draw six. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
